senses.gloss: (b. h.; √בץ; cmp. בזע, בקע, פצע)to cut, break, esp. to break bread and say the blessing.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 7b:16">Ḥull. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>מימיו לא ב׳ על וכ׳</he> never said grace over a piece of bread which was not his own (never accepted an invitation).
<cite ref="Berakhot 46a">Ber. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>בע״הב בּוֹצֵעַ וכ׳</he> the host breaks the bread and the guest says grace after meal.

<cite ref="Berakhot 47a:7">Ib. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>אין הבוצע רשאי לִבְצוֹעַ וכ׳</he> he who is chosen to break the bread, must not begin to break until the Amen of those that respond (to the blessing) is finished; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to split the difference, to adjust, compromise.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 6b:1">Snh. 6ᵇ</cite> top <he>נגמר … לבצוע</he> after the legal proceedings are closed, thou must not act as an arbiter in a compromise.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 6b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>אסור לב׳</he> the court is forbidden to attempt a settlement (you must let the law take its course).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 6b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>מצוה לב׳</he> it is a meritorious act to bring about a settlement.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 6b:5">Ib.</cite> (before having formed an opinion the judge may say) <he>צאו ובִצְעוּ</he> go out and settle; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to adjust. Y. Snh. I, 18ᵇ top המְבַצֵּעַ חוטא the judge who settles a case is a sinner.
